1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags

  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace

Browser sessions:

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish the existing Ashen Oath browser game as a complete, playable RPG.

## Requirements
- Build without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) for checks and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Kept the existing five-encounter turn-based RPG design and added synthesized Web Audio effects, gameplay guidance, and usability improvements.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed battle hit animation failure by adding the missing `hero-combatant` element ID.
- Added optional synthesized sound effects for actions, hits, victory, and defeat; updated sound toggle accessibility state.
- Added focus/action guidance, distinct final-boss heading, mobile touch behavior, visible keyboard focus, and reduced-motion support.
- Checked JavaScript syntax and diff whitespace; browser-tested class selection, starting a run, and an attack with no remaining page errors.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/opencode/ashenoath.jpg`.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked
- Standard `playwright-cli` browser launch failed because its expected Chromium installation is missing. A direct Playwright test using `/usr/bin/chromium` succeeded instead.

## Next Move
1. Optionally run broader gameplay checks through the five encounters and verify mobile layout.
2. Review and commit the uncommitted changes if appropriate.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, added sound effects and contextual action guidance.
- `index.html`: Battle combatant ID and accessible sound toggle.
- `style.css`: Touch, focus, tablet layout, and reduced-motion refinements.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Direct browser test: Knight selected, run started, Attack executed; no page errors, actions re-enabled after enemy turn.
- Screenshot: `/tmp/opencode/ashenoath.jpg`.
